faq.a: Zahir is associated with the Arabic form زَاهِر, whose core sense is zahir; shining, radiant.

faq.q: What is the origin of Zahir?
faq.a: Zahir is associated with Arabic. Zahir is Arabic زَاهِر (Zāhir), associated with the sense 'shining, radiant'. It is a different root from ظَاهِر (Ẓāhir).
Yes — the underlying form زَاهِر is Arabic.
Zahir can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zahir should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Zāhir is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Zahir mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Zahir is rendered زاہر and carries the sense زاہر، چمکتا ہوا.

faq.q: What does Zahir mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Zahir is rendered زاهر and carries the sense زاهر، درخشان.
A romanized syllable approximation is za-hir. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Zahir?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Zahir, zahir. Script forms are زاهر, زاہر, زَاهِر, ज़ाहिर.

faq.q: Is Zahir a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
